eyebrow: Deciding what to do about each issue
code:
def clean_orders(df):
    df = df.copy()
    missing_name_mask = df["customer_name"].isna()
    df.loc[missing_name_mask, "customer_name"] = "Unknown Customer"

    bad_quantity_mask = df["quantity"] <= 0
    dropped = df.loc[bad_quantity_mask, "order_id"].tolist()
    df = df[~bad_quantity_mask]

    print(f"Flagged {missing_name_mask.sum()} row(s) with unknown customer name.")
    print(f"Dropped {len(dropped)} row(s) with non-positive quantity: {dropped}")
    return df
caption: A missing name is recoverable — flag it and keep the row. A negative quantity isn't — drop it and log it.

eyebrow: Raising instead of dropping, when the stakes are higher
caption: For a pipeline feeding a billing system, silently dropping a bad row might be the wrong call entirely.
